prompt:
Create a hyper-stylized fashion dance music video with a weird, playful, chaotic mixed-media vibe.

One stylish main dancer performs a musicality-focused R&B / funk / disco-funk choreography with urban dance energy. Include body groove, shoulder groove, chest isolations, rhythmic footwork, sharp freezes, spins, pose hits, arm swings, stylish transitions, and confident attitude. The choreography must remain clear and readable.

Important rules:

Keep the original background and setting visually consistent throughout the video.

Do not replace the background with a completely different location.

Do not destroy the sense of place.

The background should remain the same base environment, while doodles, glitch effects, and mixed-media elements are added on top of it.

Do NOT draw doodles directly on the real dancer’s face.

Do NOT cover the eyes, nose, mouth, or facial features.

Keep the face clean, visible, and attractive at all times.

Doodles may appear around the head, hair outline, shoulders, arms, torso, hands, legs, and silhouette, but never directly on the face.

Special creative element:

Rough white doodle characters appear and dance together with the main dancer.

These doodle figures should feel very hand-drawn, loose, sketchy, playful, messy, and alive — like spontaneous notebook scribbles or white crayon doodles.

They should not look too clean or too polished.

They can appear as:

- simple stick-figure dancers

- rough cartoon people

- scribbled mini dancers

- stretched dancing silhouettes

- funny hand-drawn companions

- duplicated sketch clones

The doodle people interact with the real dancer in fun and surprising ways:

- dancing together in sync

- copying moves

- answering moves

- surrounding the dancer

- appearing and disappearing on the beat

- multiplying into many sketch dancers

- popping out from behind the dancer

- emerging from the floor, walls, or shadow

- briefly carrying props or reacting comedically

Also add many other rough doodle elements, not just human doodles:

- stars

- arrows

- circles

- scribbles

- lightning bolts

- speed lines

- comic impact bursts

- motion trails

- white chalk marks

- white crayon lines

- hand-drawn swirls

- rough hearts

- crossed-out marks

- check marks

- abstract symbols

- sketch smoke puffs

- dancing lines

- rough frames

- floating cartoon hands

- simple eyes or funny reaction icons

- messy graphic accents

These doodles should feel more like real doodles: rough, spontaneous, sketchy, imperfect, playful, and energetic.

Let the doodles feel handmade and a little chaotic.

Camera:

Mostly static camera with occasional smooth lateral tracking only.

The camera always stays parallel to the dancer.

The dancer remains centered in frame.

Prioritize full-body framing so the choreography is clearly visible.

No orbiting camera, no spinning camera, no drone shots, no extreme zooms, no random camera movement.

Visual style:

Premium fashion editorial look, luxury streetwear aesthetic, bold composition, high-contrast lighting, clean background, trendy music-video energy.

The real dancer and base background should feel polished and stylish, while the doodle layer feels raw, handmade, and chaotic.

This contrast is important.

Motion style:

Use a stepped low-frame-rate aesthetic inspired by stop-motion, frame-by-frame animation, cutout animation, collage animation, and animated-on-twos / animated-on-threes timing.

Add rhythmic strobing, flicker accents, pose-to-pose energy, and a 12fps-like feel while keeping the dance readable.

Extra effects:

Add glitch effects, flicker cuts, frame skipping, stutter edits, collage bursts, jittery interruptions, and chaotic beat-synced visual reactions.

Keep the choreography readable.

The weirdness should feel stylish, fun, and creative, not sloppy.

Mood:

Cool, funky, stylish, bizarre, playful, chaotic, fashion-forward, surprising, inventive, entertaining.

BGM mood:

R&B Funk, Disco Funk, Funk-pop.

No text, no subtitles, no watermark, no logo, no extra unwanted real people, no distorted anatomy, no extra limbs, no body deformation.

promptTranslations.zh:
创作一部极具风格化的时尚舞蹈音乐视频，带有古怪、俏皮且混乱的混合媒体（mixed-media）氛围。

一位时尚的主舞者演绎一段注重音乐性的 R&B / 芬克（funk）/ 迪斯科芬克（disco-funk）编舞，散发着都市街舞的活力。包括身体律动（body groove）、肩部律动（shoulder groove）、胸部孤立动作（chest isolations）、节奏感强烈的脚步动作、利落的定格（sharp freezes）、旋转、卡点造型（pose hits）、摆臂、极具格调的过渡衔接以及自信满满的气场态度。舞蹈动作必须保持清晰且易于辨识。

重要规则：

在整个视频中，保持原始背景和场景在视觉上的一致性。

切勿将背景替换为完全不同的场所。

切勿破坏空间场所感。

背景应始终保持相同的基础环境，而涂鸦、故障特效（glitch effects）和混合媒体元素则叠加在背景之上。

切勿直接在真人舞者的面部绘制涂鸦。

切勿遮挡眼睛、鼻子、嘴巴或面部特征。

时刻保持面部干净、清晰可见且富有吸引力。

涂鸦可以出现在头部周围、发型轮廓、肩膀、手臂、躯干、双手、腿部和剪影周围，但绝不能直接落在脸上。

特殊创意元素：

粗糙的白色涂鸦小人出现并与主舞者一同跳舞。

这些涂鸦形象应当具有极强的手绘感、随性、草图风、俏皮、凌乱且富有生命力——就像随手在笔记本上的涂鸦或白色蜡笔简笔画。

它们不应显得过于整洁或过度修饰。

它们可以表现为：

- 简单的火柴人舞者

- 粗线条卡通人物

- 潦草的迷你小舞者

- 拉伸变形的跳舞剪影

- 滑稽的手绘伴舞伙伴

- 复制排布的草图克隆体

涂鸦人物以有趣且出人意料的方式与真人舞者互动：

- 同步合跳

- 模仿舞步动作

- 呼应动作对答

- 环绕在舞者身边

- 随节拍卡点出现与消失

- 增殖分身成众多草图舞者

- 从舞者身后突然跳出

- 从地板、墙壁或阴影中钻出

- 短暂手持道具或做出喜剧化反应

此外还要添加大量其他粗糙的涂鸦元素，不仅限于人物涂鸦：

- 星星

- 箭头

- 圆圈

- 潦草乱线

- 闪电符号

- 速度线

- 漫画冲击爆炸光芒

- 运动轨迹拖尾

- 白粉笔笔触痕迹

- 白色蜡笔线条

- 手绘漩涡

- 粗糙爱心

- 划叉记号

- 对勾记号

- 抽象符号

- 草图烟雾团

- 律动跳跃的线条

- 粗糙线框

- 悬浮的卡通手势

- 简单的眼睛或搞笑反应表情图标

- 凌乱的图形点缀

这些涂鸦应该更有真实涂鸦的质感：粗粝、即兴、草图化、不完美、好玩且充满能量。

让涂鸦保持手作感与少许混乱感。

镜头机位：

大部分时间保持静止机位，仅偶有平滑的横向平移跟拍。

镜头始终与舞者保持平行。

舞者始终保持在画面中心。

优先采用全身构图，以便清晰看清舞蹈编排。

无环绕镜头，无旋转镜头，无无人机航拍镜头，无极端变焦，无随机镜头的晃动乱动。

视觉风格：

高端时尚大片质感，奢华街头风美学，大胆构图，高对比度布光，干净的背景，充满潮流音乐录影带的活力。

真人舞者和基础背景应精致时髦，而涂鸦层则保持原始、手作感和混乱感。

这种反差至关重要。

动态风格：

采用灵感源自定格动画（stop-motion）、逐帧动画、剪纸定格动画、拼贴动画以及一拍二/一拍三（animated-on-twos / animated-on-threes）时序的阶梯式低帧率美学。

加入富有节奏感的频闪、闪烁点缀、姿势到姿势（pose-to-pose）的爆发力，以及类似12fps的观感，同时保持舞蹈动作的易读性。

额外特效：

添加故障特效、闪烁剪辑、跳帧、卡顿剪辑、拼贴炸裂、抖动干扰以及与节拍同步的混乱视觉反应。

保持舞蹈编排动作清晰可辨。

这种怪诞感应当显得时尚、有趣且富有创造力，而非粗制滥造。

情绪氛围：

酷炫、放克、时尚、怪诞、俏皮、混乱、前卫潮流、令人惊喜、别出心裁、极具娱乐性。

背景音乐氛围：

R&B Funk、Disco Funk、Funk-pop。

无文字，无字幕，无水印，无标志，无多余不想要的真人，无解剖结构畸变，无多余肢体，无身体变形。

promptTranslations.ja-JP:
風変わりで遊び心にあふれ、カオティックなミクストメディア感を持つ、極度にスタイライズされたファッションダンスミュージックビデオを制作してください。

スタイリッシュなメインダンサー1人が、アーバンダンスのエネルギーを込めて、音楽性を重視したR&B／ファンク／ディスコファンクのコレオグラフィーを踊ります。ボディグルーヴ、ショルダールーヴ、チェストアイソレーション、リズミカルなステップワーク、キレのあるフリーズ、スピン、ポーズヒット、アームスイング、スタイリッシュなトランジション、そして自信に満ちたアティテュードを含めてください。振付は常に明確で見やすく認識できる必要があります。

重要なルール：

ビデオ全体を通して、元の背景とシチュエーションの視覚的一貫性を維持してください。

背景をまったく異なる場所に置き換えないでください。

空間の統一感や場所性を損なわないでください。

背景は同じベース環境を維持し、その上に落書き、グリッチエフェクト、ミクストメディア要素を追加してください。

実写ダンサーの顔に直接落書きを描かないでください。

目、鼻、口、顔のパーツを覆い隠さないでください。

顔は常に清潔感があり、はっきりと見え、魅力的な状態を保ってください。

頭部周辺、髪のアウトライン、肩、腕、胴体、手、脚、シルエットの周囲に落書きが現れるのは構いませんが、絶対に顔の上に直接描かないでください。

特別なクリエイティブ要素：

ラフな白い落書き（doodle）キャラクターが現れ、メインダンサーと一緒に踊ります。

- シンプルな棒人間のダンサー

- 荒々しいカートゥーン調の人物

- なぐり描きのミニダンサー

- 引き伸ばされたダンシングシルエット

- おかしな手描きの相棒たち

- 複製されたスケッチクローン

落書きキャラクターたちは、楽しく驚きのある方法で本物のダンサーとインタラクションします：

- シンクロして一緒に踊る

- 動きを真似する

- 動きに対してコール＆レスポンスする

- ダンサーを取り囲む

- ビートに合わせて現れたり消えたりする

- 無数のスケッチダンサーへと増殖する

- ダンサーの後ろからポンと飛び出す

- 床、壁、または影から湧き出る

- 短時間小道具を持ったりコミカルなリアクションをする

また、キャラクターだけでなく、他にもたくさんのラフな落書き要素を追加してください：

- 星

- 矢印

Genial, funky, elegante, bizarro, juguetón, caótico, a la vanguardia de la moda, sorprendente, ingenioso, entretenido.

R&B Funk, Disco Funk, Funk-pop.

たまにはGrokで～
可愛いのが出たので共有します。

prompt
-----
Create a hyper-stylized fashion dance music video with a weird, playful, chaotic mixed-media vibe.

One stylish main dancer performs a musicality-focused R&B / funk / disco-funk choreography with urban dance energy. Include body groove, shoulder groove, chest isolations, rhythmic footwork, sharp freezes, spins, pose hits, arm swings, stylish transitions, and confident attitude. The choreography must remain clear and readable.

Important rules:

Keep the original background and setting visually consistent throughout the video.

Do not replace the background with a completely different location.

Do not destroy the sense of place.

The background should remain the same base environment, while doodles, glitch effects, and mixed-media elements are added on top of it.

Do NOT draw doodles directly on the real dancer’s face.

Do NOT cover the eyes, nose, mouth, or facial features.

Keep the face clean, visible, and attractive at all times.

Doodles may appear around the head, hair outline, shoulders, arms, torso, hands, legs, and silhouette, but never directly on the face.

Special creative element:

Rough white doodle characters appear and dance together with the main dancer.

These doodle figures should feel very hand-drawn, loose, sketchy, playful, messy, and alive — like spontaneous notebook scribbles or white crayon doodles.

They should not look too clean or too polished.

They can appear as:

- simple stick-figure dancers

- rough cartoon people

- scribbled mini dancers

- stretched dancing silhouettes

- funny hand-drawn companions

- duplicated sketch clones

The doodle people interact with the real dancer in fun and surprising ways:

- dancing together in sync

- copying moves

- answering moves

- surrounding the dancer

- appearing and disappearing on the beat

- multiplying into many sketch dancers

- popping out from behind the dancer

- emerging from the floor, walls, or shadow

- briefly carrying props or reacting comedically

Also add many other rough doodle elements, not just human doodles:

- stars

- arrows

- circles

- scribbles

- lightning bolts

- speed lines

- comic impact bursts

- motion trails

- white chalk marks

- white crayon lines

- hand-drawn swirls

- rough hearts

- crossed-out marks

- check marks

- abstract symbols

- sketch smoke puffs

- dancing lines

- rough frames

- floating cartoon hands

- simple eyes or funny reaction icons

- messy graphic accents

These doodles should feel more like real doodles: rough, spontaneous, sketchy, imperfect, playful, and energetic.

Let the doodles feel handmade and a little chaotic.

Camera:

Mostly static camera with occasional smooth lateral tracking only.

The camera always stays parallel to the dancer.

The dancer remains centered in frame.

Prioritize full-body framing so the choreography is clearly visible.

No orbiting camera, no spinning camera, no drone shots, no extreme zooms, no random camera movement.

Visual style:

Premium fashion editorial look, luxury streetwear aesthetic, bold composition, high-contrast lighting, clean background, trendy music-video energy.

The real dancer and base background should feel polished and stylish, while the doodle layer feels raw, handmade, and chaotic.

This contrast is important.

Motion style:

Use a stepped low-frame-rate aesthetic inspired by stop-motion, frame-by-frame animation, cutout animation, collage animation, and animated-on-twos / animated-on-threes timing.

Add rhythmic strobing, flicker accents, pose-to-pose energy, and a 12fps-like feel while keeping the dance readable.

Extra effects:

Add glitch effects, flicker cuts, frame skipping, stutter edits, collage bursts, jittery interruptions, and chaotic beat-synced visual reactions.

Keep the choreography readable.

The weirdness should feel stylish, fun, and creative, not sloppy.

Mood:

Cool, funky, stylish, bizarre, playful, chaotic, fashion-forward, surprising, inventive, entertaining.

BGM mood:

R&B Funk, Disco Funk, Funk-pop.

No text, no subtitles, no watermark, no logo, no extra unwanted real people, no distorted anatomy, no extra limbs, no body deformation.
